indicators: SPF fail for sender IP 192.168.50.23 not in company.com SPF range
DMARC policy set to reject but email passed through
Email received from suspicious-mailserver.com registered only 6 days ago
Unrecognized IP sending email from executive account
Email contains base64-encoded URL parameter to suspicious domain
No DKIM signature present on purported company email
Wire transfer request not confirmed by secondary channel
Mail server logs show SPF fail rejection but email still delivered
example.detection_method: Automated email gateway inspection triggers SPF and DMARC failures, alerts raised. Security monitoring tools flag new domain registrations and unusual sender IPs for executive accounts. Network logs correlate unrecognized IP sending executive mail. SOC analysts validate wire transfer request via phone call and detect lack of confirmation. SIEM correlates mail logs, DNS queries, and user login anomalies. Behavioral analytics detect abnormal sending behavior on CEO's mailbox.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a Business Email Compromise (BEC) scenario involving executive email spoofing to request a fraudulent wire transfer. The technical data includes detailed email headers showing SPF and DMARC failures, a suspicious sending IP outside the authorized SPF range, and a recently registered suspicious domain used as the sending mailserver. The email body contains a wire transfer request consistent with BEC tactics. The sample also includes relevant logs such as SMTP transaction, mailserver logs, DNS queries, and email account activity that highlight unusual behavior and unrecognized IP usage. Indicators clearly explain why this is a BEC case, referencing authentication failures, domain age, lack of DKIM, and failure to verify the wire transfer via secondary channels. The detection methods describe a comprehensive multi-layered approach including automated gateway inspection, SOC analyst verification, and behavioral analytics, aligning well with recommended risk reduction strategies. All required fields are present and populated with realistic, plausible data. The inclusion of MITRE ATT&CK techniques further supports the scenario's validity. Overall, the sample is complete, realistic, and correctly aligned with the problem nature.
